'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[2021 Kunduz mosque bombing]]
***At least 50 people are killed and more than 100 injured when a [[suicide bomber]] targets a [[Shiite]] [[mosque]] in [[Kunduz Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|IS–K]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58842793/ (BBC News)]
*Six migrants are shot dead by guards at a [[Immigration detention|detention center]] in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], [[Libya]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/8/libya-guards-kill-migrants-shooting-libyan-detention-centre-amid-crackdown (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Public sector undertakings in India]]
**[[Tata Sons]] is announced as the winning bidder for [[Air India]], ending years of attempts by the [[government of India|government]] to privatise the loss-making airline. Tata Sons was the initial owner of the airline before it was [[Air India#As Tata Air Services|nationalised]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/business/tata-wins-control-of-air-india-once-again-with-rs-18-000-crore-bid-2568657 (NDTV)] [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/return-of-the-prodigal-son-air-india-back-in-founder-tata-fold-after-68-years/articleshow/86865871.cms ''(Times of India)'']
*[[ITA - Italia Trasporto Aereo]] is announced as the new state-owned airline for Italy, following the closure of [[Alitalia]] due to bankruptcy. ITA is a reorganization of Alitalia under a new name signed by decree in October 2020. [https://edition.cnn.com/travel/article/ita-airline-explainer/index.html (CNN)]
*The severity of the energy crisis in [[Jiangsu]], [[Zhejiang]] and [[Guangdong]] provinces of [[China]] is reported as worsening, with power outages occurring every week and "notices{{nbsp}}... telling us which days the following week that they will cut the power". Some factories report receiving power for only two or three days per week and are operating primarily on generators. China has also placed large bids for coal that are causing supply issues in locations as far away as [[Ukraine]]. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/China-tech/China-power-outages-spur-new-wave-of-supply-chain-shifts (''Nikkei Asia'')] [https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/economic/772520.html (Interfax)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Mining industry of Zimbabwe]]
**[[Gas cylinder]]s explode at a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] in [[Mazowe]], [[Zimbabwe]], killing seven people and injuring another. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/seven-die-gas-explosion-zimbabwe-gold-mine-police-say-2021-10-08/ (Reuters)]
*At least 51 people are dead after their makeshift vessel sinks in the [[Congo River]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. Several more are missing. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/9/over-100-dead-or-missing-after-vessel-capsizes-in-dr-congo (Al Jazeera)]
*Five people are killed by [[flash flood]]ing occurs in parts of the U.S. states of [[Alabama]] and [[Tennessee]], with as much as 13 inches of rain falling in some areas. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/child-killed-alabama-flooding-latest-forecast/story?id=80453319 (ABC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/06/weather/alabama-flash-flooding-birmingham/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]] reports that the [[USS Connecticut (SSN-22)|USS ''Connecticut'']], a nuclear-powered fast-attack submarine, struck an unidentified object while submerged in the [[South China Sea]], causing 11 crew members to be injured. The extent of the damage to the [[Seawolf-class submarine|''Seawolf''-class submarine]] is still being assessed although the submarine is noted as being "safe and stable". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-08/eleven-hurt-in-u-s-sub-crash-in-south-china-sea-report-says (Bloomberg)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****[[President of Cyprus|President]] [[Nicos Anastasiades]] receives a [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.financialmirror.com/2021/10/08/covid19-president-gets-booster-jab/ (''Financial Mirror'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Iceland]]
****[[Iceland]] suspends the use of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] due to concerns of side effects, becoming the fourth European country to do so. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-08/iceland-joins-nordic-peers-in-halting-moderna-covid-vaccinations (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 936 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 214,485. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/coronavirus-deaths-in-russia-hit-new-record/2021/10/08/8ec066a8-2831-11ec-8739-5cb6aba30a30_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] grants conditional approval for the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] to be used as a [[booster dose]] for people over the age of 18 years old who received their second dose at least six months ago. [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/southeast-asia/malaysia-pfizer-biontech-booster-shots-b1934704.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 3,590 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 120,454. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/6-more-covid-19-deaths-in-singapore-bringing-toll-to-142-3590-new-infections (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record 1,838 new cases and five deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total of new [[COVID-19]] cases of any [[Australian state]] or territory since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-08/victoria-covid-cases-school-student-mask-mandate-vaccine-target/100522902 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] surpasses 600,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.voanews.com/a/brazil-passes-600-000-covid-deaths-second-only-to-us-/6263090.html (VOA)]
*Authorities in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] announce that a 3-year-old boy who died last Wednesday in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]] tested positive for [[Ebola]]. The health minister could not confirm if this was related to the [[Kivu Ebola outbreak]] which ended in 2020 and killed more than 2,200 people, but said that they were closely monitoring 100 people who may have been exposed to the virus and that three boys, all of whom were neighbors of the toddler, were already showing symptoms of the disease. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/new-ebola-case-confirmed-eastern-congo-lab-report-2021-10-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Nobel Peace Prize]]
**Journalists [[Maria Ressa]] of the [[Philippines]] and [[Dmitry Muratov]] of [[Russia]] are awarded the [[Nobel Peace Prize]] "for their efforts to safeguard the [[freedom of expression]]". [https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/maria-ressa-and-dmitry-muratov-win-2021-nobel-peace-prize-1862343-2021-10-08 (AFP via ''India Today'')]
*[[Politics of Austria]]
**The [[Green Party of Austria|Green Party]], a [[left-wing]] member of the [[coalition]], says that [[Chancellor of Austria|Chancellor]] [[Sebastian Kurz]] is "unfit" for the position as he is investigated for [[corruption]]. The party demands that Kurz step down, although Kurz has denied any wrongdoing. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/austrias-government-teeters-greens-seek-options-oust-kurz-2021-10-08/ (Reuters)]
*In his first speech, [[Prime Minister of Japan|Japanese prime minister]] [[Fumio Kishida]] vows to fight and end the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|COVID-19 pandemic]] and counter the [[government of China|Chinese]] and [[government of North Korea|North Korean]] threats by strengthening [[Japan coast guard]] and [[missile defense]]s while maintaining the country's peace. Kishida also vows to strengthen [[Japan–United States relations|the country's alliance]] with the [[United States]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/8/japans-new-pm-promises-to-do-his-utmost-to-end-covid-19-crisis (Al Jazeera)]
*The United States [[House Oversight Committee]] releases documents showing that the [[Old Post Office (Washington, D.C.)#Trump International Hotel Washington, D.C.|Trump International Hotel]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] accumulated [[United States dollar|$]]70 million in losses while public financial disclosures claimed that the hotel was producing an income of $156 million for former [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]]. [[General Services Administration]] documents also showed that Trump received "undisclosed preferential treatment" from [[Deutsche Bank]] on a $170 million construction loan during his presidency. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/08/politics/trump-hotel-dc/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-organization-hid-payments-foreign-governments-us-house-panel-alleges-2021-10-08/ (Reuters)]
